Can you spot the melanoma? 👀

#melanoma #melanomaawareness #skincancer #skincancerawareness #greenscreen

on_screen_hook: Which of these four spots is a melanoma? Let's use dermoscopy to
transcript: Which of these four spots is a melanoma? Let's use dermoscopy to figure it out. Lesion 1 is a tiny flat, immensely pigmented, almost jet black macule. The degree of pigmentation can certainly look concerning. Dermoscopy shows a strikingly dark reticular pigment network that is sharply defined and mostly regular and organized, almost as if somebody dropped ink onto the skin. Diagnosis, ink spot lentigo. This one's benign. Lesion 2 is an irregularly shaped, deeply pigmented blue black macule on melanin rich skin, which clinically can certainly raise concern. Dermoscopy reveals a homogeneous structureless blue pigmentation. That blue colour likely represents melanin deeper in the dermis due to the Tyndall effect. Diagnosis: blue nevus. This one's also benign. Lesion 3, another dark, irregularly shaped macule. At First glance this almost looks like a pigment network but if you look closer, this is not a true melanocytic network. These are non melanocytic structures including fissures, ridges, milia like cysts and comedolike openings. Diagnosis, a benign sebaceous keratosis. With a naked eye, lesion 4 already has asymmetry, an irregular border, multiple colours including pink, brown and black and a growing diameter. On dermatoscopy, we can appreciate a true reticular melanocytic network at the periphery along with an architectural disorder, irregular pigmentation, areas of regression, irregular dots and globules, scar like depigmentation and areas of grey peppering. This is a melanoma in situ. Clinically pigmented lesions can look strikingly similar and even an expert eye may need a biopsy to confirm the Diagnosis, but dermoscopy brings us much closer to diagnostic certainty and helps us detect melanoma much earlier among its mimickers.

title: Celebs Caught With Ozempic Face | Then vs Now
caption:
Celebrities before & after the “Ozempic Face” debate… 😳

Fans are comparing dramatic before-and-after photos and discussing how rapid weight loss may change facial appearance.

#shorts #ozempic #celebritynews #beforeandafter #transformation #viral #trending #hollywood
transcript: Sharon Osborn lost so much weight that she admitted she could barely recognize her own face. After using Osempic, Sharon said she became too gaunt and even struggled to regain weight. Fans immediately noticed her hollow cheeks, sharper jawline, and dramatic loss of facial volume. One of the most talked about examples of what's now called Osempic face. Then there's Whoopi Goldberg. Whoopi openly admitted she used Monjaro after her weight reached nearly 300 pounds. Her transformation shocked fans, but it also sparked conversations about how rapid weight loss can dramatically change facial appearance. Next is Kathy Bates. Kathy lost around 100 pounds and later explained that while Osempic helped, it wasn't the whole story. Fans immediately noticed her face looked much slimmer with more defined features and less facial volume than before. Then there's Rosie O'Donnell. Rosie revealed she was using Monjaro and said it completely changed her appetite. As the weight came off, fans also noticed a much leaner, more angular appearance compared to previous years. Joy Behar also surprised viewers. After revealing she lost around 25 pounds using Osempic, fans began comparing before and after photos pointing to a noticeably slimmer face alongside her weight loss. And finally, Kelly Osbourne. Kelly has repeatedly denied using Osempic for her weight loss, but her dramatically slimmer appearance has fueled non-stop online speculation. Fans continue debating her transformation every time new photos surface. Even though she has pushed back against the rumors. But here's what most people don't realize. Osempic face isn't actually caused by the medication itself. Doctors say it's the result of rapid weight loss, which can reduce facial fat, making cheeks appear hollow and facial features look more defined or older. The same effect can happen after any significant weight loss, not just with GLP1 medications.

transcript: Esto elimina cualquier mancha al instante y ella lo enseñó en vivo. El melasma es una enfermedad sistémica, no solo de la piel. No sirve de nada hacerse peelings, láser, ni un montón de procedimientos. Tenemos que tratarlo de adentro hacia afuera. Este soy yo, llorando por el melasma hace cuatro años y miren cómo estaba mi rostro. Quienes me han acompañado en los últimos meses saben cuánto sufrí y cuánto dinero gasté intentando tratarme. Y me duele recordarlo. Tratamientos caros en clínicas, rutinas agotadoras de skincare con productos que no eran nada baratos. No voy a mentir, algunos de esos productos y métodos sí me ayudaron. Pero el problema era que mis manchas siempre volvían y todavía más oscuras. Miren cómo está mi rostro ahora, después de cuatro meses. Prácticamente sin manchas, aquí te enseño la receta. Corta un limón por la mitad y con la piel limpia y seca, coloca sobre una de las mitades una capa fina de vaselina y una cucharadita pequeña de café molido, mezcla ligeramente sobre el mismo limón. Luego, pásalo suavemente sobre las manchas con movimientos circulares durante dos a tres minutos. Deja actuar de 10 a 15 minutos, enjuaga con agua tibia y aplica hidratante. Úsalo solo por la noche, dos o tres veces por semana y evita el sol después de aplicarlo. Si quieres un protocolo para una digestión ligera, comenta guía y te la envió por interno.
